title: Who keeps the forest alive?
content:
I returned last week from Antalya, where we launched two pieces of work with the Brazilian government. The first, written with Minister Esther Dweck, looks at how governments can use public procurement to deliver on the Belém Declaration on Sustainable Public Procurement, a commitment made at COP30 to use the purchasing power of governments to support sustainable production. Our policy report, The Belém Declaration on Sustainable Public Procurement: from commitment to implementation, sets out how, and I make the wider argument in Project Syndicate. The second, The Living Forest Economy: Putting Forest Peoples at the Centre of the Economy, is co-authored with Edel Moraes, Brazil’s National Secretary for Traditional Peoples and Communities and Sustainable Rural Development, and is the subject of this post. In Antalya, Edel Moraes and I met with colleagues from Brazil’s Ministry of the Environment and Climate Change to discuss this work.
